titleStmt.title: Telegram From Secretary of State Shultz’s Delegation to the Department of State and the White House

div.head: 458. Telegram From Secretary of State Shultz’s Delegation to the Department of State and the White House
div.p: Secto 15030. Subject: Memorandum for the President: Uruguay, August 4.
Subject: My day in Uruguay, August 4, 1988.

3. The old line about Uruguay is that when either of its (comparatively) huge neighbors, Argentina or Brazil, sneeze, Uruguay catches cold. Right now, though, they are sneezing and sniffling and Uruguay is managing to stay pretty healthy.

4. Certainly Uruguay is ahead of both Brazil and Argentina in opening up its economy and in restoring a relaxed, totally open democratic system. It is a good example of the latter that Pres. Sanguinetti invited to his luncheon for me the leaders of all the opposition parties—and they all came.

5. Sanguinetti is, as you will recall from his state visit in 1986, a very perceptive and equally charming man. He has managed Uruguay’s transition to democracy brilliantly, and travelled the world to bring recognition to his small country. He has a realistic view of the Sandinistas, wants to be helpful on Panama if there’s anything constructive Uruguay can do, and offers some real insights about countries as varied as Chile and the Soviet Union. Here, as in Argentina, the return to democracy has brought to the fore a team of very impressive leaders. The consolidation of democracy seems secure, and if they can succeed with their economic plans they’ll give some meaning to the old description of Uruguay as the Switzerland of Latin
America.

note.p: Source: Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, N880006–0059. Secret; Immediate; Nodis. Sent from aboard the delegation’s aircraft. Shultz travelled to Montevideo to meet with Sanguinetti and senior Uruguayan officials, August 4. He also gave an address to businessmen and bankers and gave a news conference; see Department of State Bulletin, October 1988, pp. 2–20.

In telegram 4953 from Montevideo, August 5, the Embassy transmitted the text of Shultz’s August 4 press conference in Montevideo. (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D880683–0333)

No memorandum of conversation has been found. In telegram 5057 from Montevideo, August 9, the Embassy reported on Shultz’s August 4 meeting with Uruguayan political officials at the Ambassador’s residence. (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D880695–0318)

In telegram 4985 from Montevideo, August 5, the Embassy reported on Shultz’s August 4 meeting with Barrios Tassano in which they discussed Panama, writing: “After both the Secretary and Barrios Tassano had explored every development in the U.S.-Noriega imbroglio, the situation was left that Barrios Tassano and Sanguinetti would use their best efforts to obtain from the Noriega regime a statement of the terms and conditions on which Noriega would depart, and would keep the Ambassador in Montevideo fully informed of any developments.” (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D880683–0717)

In telegram 5042 from Montevideo, August 9, the Embassy reported on Shultz’s August 4 meeting with Zerbino in which they discussed “market-oriented measures undertaken by the Sanguinetti administration; Zerbino’s thoughts on the Uruguay Round; Zerbino’s apprehension regarding the U.S. trade bill; the seventh replenishment of the IDB; and the upcoming bilateral textile negotiations in Washington.” (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D880695–0027)
